A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same provenance-testing study. Their complete main texts, appendices, algorithms, tables and figures support comparison despite substantial reorganization and formatting changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on BENCH-A and BENCH-B, including precision/recall, control-set sensitivity, query reduction and known-parent testing.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a significance-level sensitivity experiment in Appendix G.

M1.justification: Next-token agreement, control-model comparisons, z-tests, Holm-Bonferroni correction, rejection sampling and Best Arm Identification are retained. All four algorithms match after renumbering and relocation; the condensed explanations do not establish an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same BENCH-A and BENCH-B collections and known-parent/unspecified-parent tasks. v2 Table 5 identifies domain-specific models already included in those benchmarks; it does not establish added datasets, domains or test scenarios.

E2.justification: v2 Section 4.2 adds a quantitative random-parent-guessing reference: calculated precision of approximately 0.09 for BENCH-A and 0.02 for BENCH-B. This comparison was absent from v1's unspecified-parent evaluation. Base-versus-BAI comparisons remain unchanged; the new literature table introduces no empirically tested competitors.

E3.justification: v2 Appendix G adds a BENCH-A evaluation varying alpha over 0.01, 0.05 and 0.1. The default remains 0.05, and existing benchmark construction, prompt generation, control-set experiments, query budgets and known-parent pair construction are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix G and Figure 7 newly examine sensitivity of precision and recall to the significance threshold. Existing analyses of parent similarity, control-set size, prompt randomness, rejection sampling, BAI and known-parent testing remain, sometimes relocated or combined.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same five independently sampled prompt-set runs and 100 repetitions per control-set size. Statistical tests, multiple-testing correction and uncertainty-reporting practices remain unchanged. The added alpha sweep is a sensitivity experiment, not a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds precision/recall curves for the alpha sweep and reports limited sensitivity over the tested range. Known-parent precision traces also change slightly between v1 Figures 6–7 and v2 Figure 6, without a stated protocol change. Main accuracy curves, BAI results, five-run results and rejection-sampling table values are retained.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1 Section 3.1's formal fixed-vocabulary model setup and explicit temperature-zero/argmax assumption, including its repeated-sampling argument for higher temperatures. Similarity definitions, hypotheses, Holm-Bonferroni formulas and the BAI confidence-radius formula remain unchanged; no new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: v2 newly claims that the approach and its false-positive guarantee are agnostic to the chosen closeness metric, particularly in the contributions and related-work discussion. The central black-box provenance claim and headline precision/recall claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v1 describes adaptive obfuscation as a significant challenge beyond its scope. v2 instead questions its benefit, citing random prompts and possible task-performance costs, although evaluation remains non-adaptive. v2 also explicitly acknowledges that alternative control-selection strategies were not evaluated; the principal similarity and baseline limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a repository link for the implementation and benchmarks and lists domain-specific model identifiers and access URLs in Table 5. Hardware, software and prompt-generation details are retained after relocation. The explicit decoding and higher-temperature sampling guidance from v1 disappears.

R1.justification: v2 substantially replaces v1's broad ownership, statistical-security and customization discussion with detailed fingerprinting/watermarking positioning. Section 2.1 and Appendix A add comparisons involving LLMmap, REEF, Mergeprint and other approaches, including a new table contrasting access requirements, techniques and additional knowledge.

P1.justification: The overview, motivation, problem setup and methodological explanations are extensively condensed and reorganized. Related work moves near the beginning and expands into an appendix; the basic tester and experimental setup move to appendices. This changes the narrative substantially beyond ordinary copyediting.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the two-column layout with a single-column format and extensively resizes and rearranges displays. It redraws the schematic and plot styling, combines the known-parent figures and model-list tables, and adds related-work, domain-example and alpha-sensitivity displays. Several plots become markedly more compressed.

improvement.justification: The new alpha sensitivity check, more specific fingerprinting comparisons and code/benchmark access information modestly strengthen validation, positioning and reproducibility information. These gains are partly offset by omitted decoding assumptions, less cautious adaptive-evasion discussion and compressed figures. The core method and principal empirical evidence remain largely unchanged.
